capability_map.engine_version_verified: v4.22.1 (graph module ver 42201), confirmed live via MODULE LIST against falkordb/falkordb:latest on 2026-10-18

primitives.name: openCypher multi-hop traversal (variable-length paths)
primitives.can: Variable-length patterns -[:REL*1..3]-> with literal bounds; named paths p=(a)-[*..]->(b) returning full path objects; shortestPath(); pattern predicates in WHERE; UNWIND over path nodes.
primitives.cant: The variable-length bound CANNOT be a query parameter: -[:E*1..$d]-> fails with 'Encountered unhandled type in inlined properties'. Depth must be string-interpolated, which is an injection surface. Unnamed relationship patterns only verify existence - you cannot read properties off them without binding a variable.
primitives.evidence: docs.falkordb.com/cypher/ + live GRAPH.QUERY probes on v4.22.1
primitives.load_bearing_for: The core retrieval path. This is THE primitive that a flat vector store structurally cannot replicate - it is the honest answer to the 'is the graph decoration?' disqualifier.

primitives.name: Vector index (HNSW) + vecf32 KNN
primitives.can: CREATE VECTOR INDEX on node/relationship properties; db.idx.vector.queryNodes(label, prop, k, vecf32([...])) returning (node, score); 32-bit float vectors; cosine/euclidean.
primitives.cant: Vector queries combine poorly with property filters - pre-filtering is not pushed into the index, so you over-fetch then filter in Cypher. Issue #2233: a plain Python list silently bypasses the index (no error, full scan, wrong-looking results). Issue #2848: concurrent KNN queries can return duplicate nodes.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Entry-point retrieval (semantic seed nodes) that then hands off to traversal. NOT load-bearing alone - a vector-only design is exactly the 'graph is decoration' failure.

primitives.name: Full-text index (RediSearch-backed)
primitives.can: CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex / queryNodes; scoring; phonetic matching; stopword config.
primitives.cant: Prefix matching only at the END of a word (foo* works, *foo does not). Issue #3248 open. No fuzzy matching knob exposed at the Cypher layer.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Lexical fallback for entity lookup when embeddings miss exact identifiers (IDs, names, code symbols).

primitives.name: Built-in graph algorithms (11, CORRECTED by live dbms.procedures() probe)
primitives.can: algo.AStar, algo.BFS, algo.HarmonicCentrality, algo.MSF, algo.SPpaths (single-pair), algo.SSpaths (single-source), algo.WCC, algo.betweenness, algo.labelPropagation, algo.maxFlow, algo.pageRank. All callable via CALL and composable with MATCH. maxFlow is natively multi-source/multi-sink: algo.maxFlow({relationshipTypes:[one], sourceNodes:[], targetNodes:[], capacityProperty:'cap'}) YIELD maxFlow, nodes. algo.SPpaths({sourceNode, targetNode, relTypes, weightProp}) YIELD path, pathWeight. algo.pageRank takes TWO POSITIONAL args (label, relType), not a config map. Measured: maxFlow on a 1402-node / 2400-edge node-split DAG = 41ms cold, 11ms warm.
primitives.cant: CORRECTION 2026-10-18: algo.dijkstra and algo.SCC DO NOT EXIST in v4.22.1 - the earlier map listed both and was wrong. Weighted shortest path is algo.SPpaths with weightProp. Also NO Louvain/Leiden, NO triangle count, NO node2vec/embeddings. NO stored procedures of any kind (no CREATE PROCEDURE) - algo.* are engine built-ins only. maxFlow over unit-capacity EDGES counts EDGE-disjoint paths, so vertex-disjointness (true source independence) requires manual node-splitting in the schema.
primitives.maturity: GA (algorithm list re-derived live; prior map was partly fabricated from docs)
primitives.evidence: CALL dbms.procedures() on falkordb/falkordb:v4.22.1, 2026-10-18, plus timed GRAPH.RO_QUERY probes
primitives.load_bearing_for: Judge-visible 'real graph work'. Roi Lipman (CTO) personally authored the pathfinding post two days before the hackathon - algo.dijkstra/AStar/SPpaths usage is the highest-signal sponsor alignment available.

primitives.name: CCH (Customizable Contraction Hierarchies) index
primitives.can: Preprocesses a weighted graph so repeated shortest-path queries answer orders of magnitude faster; the subject of FalkorDB's 2026-10-12 engineering post.
primitives.cant: Exists in 4.x only; ABSENT from the 6.0 line. Preprocessing cost is non-trivial and must be re-run on graph mutation - bad fit for a graph written to continuously at demo time.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Only load-bearing for a mostly-static weighted graph with heavy repeated pathfinding. NOT suitable for a continuously-mutating memory graph.

primitives.name: Multi-graph namespace (select_graph) + GRAPH.COPY
primitives.can: Many independent named graphs in one instance; GRAPH.COPY clones a whole graph server-side (useful for snapshot/branch/rollback demos); per-graph GRAPH.DELETE.
primitives.cant: NO cross-graph queries. A single Cypher statement cannot touch two graphs. This makes any 'shared memory across isolated agents' design a REAL architectural problem, not a config flag - you either co-locate agents in one graph with ownership edges, or you build an application-layer merge.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Multi-agent memory topology. The no-cross-graph limit is the constraint that forces a genuine design decision - and is therefore the differentiator surface for Track 02.

primitives.name: GRAPH.RO_QUERY (read-only enforcement)
primitives.can: Server-side rejection of any write in the query; the correct primitive for exposing an LLM-generated Cypher path safely.
primitives.cant: Exposed in the Python client only. The TypeScript client has no ro_query binding (issue #408 open) - a TS stack must send the raw command through the Redis connection itself.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Safety boundary for any agent-writes-its-own-Cypher feature. Without it, LLM-authored Cypher can DELETE the memory graph.

primitives.name: Constraints (unique / mandatory)
primitives.can: GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE for UNIQUE and MANDATORY on node/relationship properties; backed by an exact-match index.
primitives.cant: NO Cypher DDL - constraints are a separate Redis command, not CREATE CONSTRAINT. Creation is ASYNC and returns status PENDING; you must poll GRAPH.CONSTRAINT LIST until ACTIVE or writes race the constraint. Failure mode is silent if you do not poll.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Entity-resolution integrity (one canonical node per real-world entity). Essential if dedup is part of the story.

primitives.name: TTL / expiry
primitives.can: Redis EXPIRE on the graph KEY works - a whole graph can be given a lifetime (undocumented but verified live).
primitives.cant: NO per-node or per-edge TTL. Memory decay/forgetting must be implemented in application logic (timestamp property + a sweeper query). There is no engine-level forgetting primitive despite 'memory' being the hackathon theme.
primitives.evidence: live EXPIRE probe on a test graph key, v4.22.1
primitives.load_bearing_for: Decay/compaction. Because the engine gives nothing here, a measured forgetting policy is unclaimed whitespace rather than a built-in.

primitives.name: Python client falkordb 1.8.0
primitives.can: Sync + async; select_graph; query/ro_query; parameterized queries; connection pooling via redis-py; Sentinel support.
primitives.cant: NO retries by default - a single transient connection error surfaces as an exception mid-demo (issue #306). No py.typed marker, so mypy/pyright see it as untyped (issue #269). Parameters cannot be used for labels, relationship types, or var-length bounds.
primitives.load_bearing_for: The application data layer. Wrap every call in an explicit retry - this is a known demo-killer.

primitives.name: GraphRAG-SDK 1.4.0
primitives.can: Ontology auto-detection from unstructured sources, KG construction, LLM-backed chat over the graph; the sponsor's own flagship toolkit.
primitives.cant: OPENLY BROKEN on 6.0.x (issue #344) with a 30-second circuit-breaker lockout on failure, which makes debugging brutal. Opinionated ontology layer that fights any hand-designed schema. Heavy LLM call volume per ingest.
primitives.load_bearing_for: NOT RECOMMENDED as load-bearing. Using it is sponsor-aligned but puts a known-fragile dependency on the critical path of a 7-hour build.

primitives.name: FalkorDB MCP Server 1.3.0 (7 tools)
primitives.can: Exposes list-graphs / schema / query / ro-query etc. to any MCP client; the fastest path to 'an agent talks to the graph'.
primitives.cant: Table stakes, not differentiation - it appears in ~41% of scanned competitor repos. Issue #192: binds 0.0.0.0 by default (do not expose on the deploy host without a bind override).
primitives.evidence: docs.falkordb.com/integration/mcp-server.html; issue #192; roster scan of 267 hackathon repos
primitives.load_bearing_for: Agent<->graph transport. Fine to use, cannot BE the idea.

primitives.name: FalkorDB Browser UI (port 3000)
primitives.can: Visual graph explorer bundled in the same container; good for a demo-video B-roll shot.
primitives.cant: EXPLICITLY NOT LOAD-BEARING. Official rules: 'The graph must perform essential functions, not merely visualize data.' Leaning on the browser UI as the product is the single most direct route to the decoration disqualifier.
primitives.load_bearing_for: NOTHING. Demo garnish only - deliberately flagged as non-load-bearing.

primitives.name: Persistence / durability
primitives.can: RDB snapshots at dir=/var/lib/falkordb/data, dbfilename=dump.rdb, save='3600 1 300 100 60 10000'. Survives container restart when a volume is mounted.
primitives.cant: The image declares NO VOLUME, and appendonly=no by default - worst case 60 seconds of writes lost, and everything lost on docker rm without an explicit -v. FalkorDB Cloud free tier has NO persistence and NO backups, idle-stops at 1 day, deletes at 7, and no judging date is published.
primitives.evidence: live CONFIG GET + docker image inspect on falkordb/falkordb:latest
primitives.load_bearing_for: The live-deployment submission artifact. Self-host with -v falkordb_data:/var/lib/falkordb/data --appendonly yes; the seed script in the repo is the real durability guarantee.

primitives.name: Flex UDF library (string similarity)
primitives.can: levenshtein(), jaroWinkler() and friends callable directly in Cypher for fuzzy string comparison.
primitives.cant: Thin library, sparsely documented, no fuzzy INDEX - similarity is computed per-row at query time, so it does not scale past a candidate set you have already narrowed.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Entity resolution / dedup - the cheap in-engine way to merge 'Dami' and 'Damilola' without an extra LLM call.

primitives.name: GRAPH.RO_QUERY (read-only execution boundary)
primitives.can: Server-side rejection of ANY write in the submitted Cypher. Verified: CREATE -> 'graph.RO_QUERY is to be executed only on read-only queries'; MATCH ... RETURN count(n) -> allowed.
primitives.cant: The TypeScript client does not expose it (issue #408); from TS it is reachable only by sending the raw Redis command. Python client exposes it directly.
primitives.load_bearing_for: The only real containment boundary for LLM-authored Cypher - server-side, not client-side validation.

primitives.name: db.idx.cch.query (Customizable Contraction Hierarchies index)
primitives.can: Present in dbms.procedures() on v4.22.1 - the index surface behind the 2026-10-12 Dijkstra/A*/CCH blog post by Lipman.
primitives.cant: Undocumented signature; not exercised in this build.
primitives.load_bearing_for: Nothing in this build; recorded because it is sponsor-newest (L5) surface area.

organizer_feedback.friction: docker pull falkordb/falkordb:latest resolves to v4.22.1 (graph module ver 42201) even though the 6.0.0 release notes state latest now points at 6.0. Anyone following the quickstart gets 4.x while reading 6.x docs.
The official WeMakeDevs tutorial 'How to build an agent that reasons over a graph' contains a flagship query that does not run as written on the pinned image.

Passing a plain Python list (instead of vecf32()) to a vector query silently bypasses the HNSW index - no error, no warning, just a full scan and wrong-shaped results. Silent data-correctness failure.
Concurrent KNN queries return duplicate nodes.
GraphRAG-SDK - the sponsor's own flagship toolkit - is broken against FalkorDB 6.0.x and fails into a 30-second circuit-breaker lockout, which makes iterating on the error nearly impossible.

Variable-length path bounds cannot be parameterized: -[:E*1..$depth]-> raises 'Encountered unhandled type in inlined properties'. Forces string interpolation into Cypher, i.e. an injection surface, for the single most common graph operation.
Constraint creation is async and returns PENDING with no blocking option; callers must poll GRAPH.CONSTRAINT LIST or silently race their own writes.
The TypeScript client has no GRAPH.RO_QUERY binding, so the read-only safety boundary is unavailable to the JS ecosystem exactly where LLM-generated Cypher is most likely to be executed.
The Python client performs no retries by default; one transient reconnect raises mid-request. Every quickstart omits retry handling.
The Docker image declares no VOLUME and ships appendonly=no, so the documented quickstart (docker run --rm) loses the entire graph with no warning. Nothing in getting-started mentions persistence.
organizer_feedback.evidence: docker image inspect + CONFIG GET appendonly, live

organizer_feedback.friction: algo.maxFlow's capacityProperty argument is documented incorrectly; the documented call signature errors.
Full-text prefix matching works only at the end of a word; no suffix or infix matching, and the limitation is not stated in the indexing docs.
falkordb-py ships without a py.typed marker, so the package is invisible to mypy/pyright in strict projects.
POSITIVE: docs.falkordb.com publishes a well-formed llms.txt, which made machine-reading the whole doc surface fast and accurate. Worth keeping and worth other sponsors copying.

algo.SPpaths SILENTLY IGNORES wrong weight-key names. weightProperty, relationshipWeightProperty and costProperty all return the UNWEIGHTED hop count instead of erroring; only weightProp is honoured. A build that guessed the key ships a 'weighted' score that is secretly hop-count, and every test passes.

algo.maxFlow's config keys are undocumented and error opaquely ('MaxFlow configuration contains unknown key') without naming the accepted set. Recovered only by bisection across ten guesses. relationshipTypes must contain exactly one type.
Docs reference algo.dijkstra and algo.SCC; neither exists in v4.22.1. The authoritative list is only obtainable from CALL dbms.procedures() against the running engine.

key_findings.track_crowding: Roster audit of 384 FalkorDB-mentioning repos created on/after 2026-10-14 (267 with explicit hackathon markers): Track 01 'Agents That Act on Connected Data' = 71 sole-track repos (HIGH/red ocean); Track 03 'Company Brain' = 33 (HIGH); Track 02 'Agent Memory and Coordination' = 17 (MEDIUM, a 4.2x gap below Track 01). Only 18 repos have BOTH a deploy and a video. KICKOFF.md section 3 guessed Company Brain was most crowded - that inference is WRONG; Track 01 is. KICKOFF section 4's conclusion (favour agent memory) survives, but for a different and now-evidenced reason.
key_findings.prior_art_warning: The KICKOFF section 4 recommended direction - 'an agent that writes experience into a FalkorDB graph and does multi-hop retrieval' - is NOT novel. It is `pip install graphiti-core[falkordb]`. FalkorDB publishes first-party integration docs for Graphiti, Cognee, Mem0 and a Graphiti MCP server. Shipping that shape unmodified is a reimplementation the judges (who wrote those docs) will recognise in seconds.
key_findings.phase_3_revision: SUPERSEDES the phase_1 wedge ranking. The named-competitor sweep (15 repos profiled) found that SHARED MULTI-AGENT MEMORY IS ITSELF TABLE STAKES - at least 8 hackathon entries state it verbatim in their repo description. Contradiction DETECTION is also occupied (MOHITPRADHAN35/agentmesh owns the literal [:CONTRADICTS] + (:Conflict) vocabulary). Provenance-trust scoring has one serious occupant (HamzaShaikh-source/Quorum-falkordb, the best-executed entry in the entire 100-repo set). WHAT REMAINS CLEAR: the ARBITRATION FUNCTION - a composite of corroboration-depth x recency x source-trust, computed IN CYPHER, that autonomously names a winner between two UNCORRECTED rival assertions. agentmesh preserves both; ninaivu/Graphiti/Zep/TOKI pick the newer; Mem0 defers to the reader LLM; Cognee defers to LLM judgement; Quorum propagates truth supplied externally by a human correction and states its ranking blend lives in the API process, not Cypher. Dami ruled this direction at the SPRINT planning-converge checkpoint, 2026-10-18 12:10 WAT.
differentiation_wedges: RULED (Dami, 2026-10-18): autonomous Cypher-native arbitration over provenance chains. NOT 'shared memory' as such - that is table stakes. Two standing warnings: agentmesh owns the detection vocabulary (differentiate on arbitration-vs-detection in the README's first line), and Quorum will out-polish on execution (59+ commits, 660+ tests, CI) so lead with the arbitration demo it structurally cannot show.

Write-time verification / provenance gate. HaluMem measured <60% extraction recall across all four tested memory systems - i.e. memory systems silently drop and fabricate facts at write time. Nobody gates the write.
Local/small-model-safe extraction (works without a frontier LLM on the ingest path).
Forgetting / compaction with a MEASURED tradeoff curve - the engine offers no per-node TTL, so this is unclaimed.
Honest reproducible eval against a named benchmark (LongMemEval / LOCOMO / HaluMem / agent-memory-bench, the last being FalkorDB's own, published 2 days ago).
key_findings.blog_prize_whitespace: 65 DEV.to posts exist under the falkordb tag. Many report FalkorDB bugs incidentally; NONE is the consolidated 'FalkorDB sharp edges and how to work around them' post. The organizer_feedback array above is a live-verified 16-entry draft of exactly that post. Low-cost second shot at the AirPods bounty.
key_findings.judging_shape: No live demo, no call - judges score the submitted artifacts and nothing else [B2]. The README + demo video + form prose ARE the product. Likely panel = FalkorDB's own engineers (Korland, Lipman, Avni, Zhang) + a WeMakeDevs staffer. Lipman published the pathfinding post 6 days before the deadline; Zhang published the agent-memory post on day 2 of the hackathon. Real algorithm usage and latency numbers are the highest-signal moves available.
key_findings.multi_track_upside: Rules section 5 permits one project to enter multiple tracks, but every entered track must be named at submission. Free expected-value upside - declare Track 02 primary and whichever others the build honestly satisfies.
